newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo business delegation in New York May 27.
newsitem.headline: Yugo business delegation in New York May 27.

text.p: A 10-member Yugoslav business delegation will visit New York on May 27, president of the U.S.-F.R. Yugoslavia Economic Council John Scanlan said on Friday.
"The U.S.-F.R Yugoslavia Business Council invited the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce and Industry to New York on May 27," Scanlan told a business gathering in Belgrade.

"There is a considerable interest among the United States' businessmen in pursuing the dialogue with their potential Yugoslav partners about future business opportunities. We expect a good turnout by the U.S. side at the May 27 meeting," he added.

Her acknowledged that soured relations between Belgrade and Washington in the aftermath of the Yugoslav civil war stood in the way to normal business relations. He also appeared to criticise the remaining economic sanctions that separate Belgrade from normal relations with the West.
"The bad news is that the political dialogue between our two countries has not yet developed to the point that would facilitate a significant increase in business activity."

"However, we must understand that politics and politicians are a reality. I personally am against the economic sanctions because they always hurt the wrong people and never produce desired effects. But if they are imposed they are a reality that must be dealt with," Scanlan said.
Scanlan made clear it was up to authorities in Belgrade to improve the situation.

"The U.S.-F.R. Yugoslavia Business Council would like to see this change. We would like to see the political atmosphere for doing business with and in Yugoslavia change. But as we say in America, the ball is in your court."

Belgrade's full return to the world community has been made conditional on its co-operation with the Hague war crimes tribunal, respect for human rights in its mostly-Albanian southern Kosovo province and progress in talks on dividing former Yugoslavia's assets. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
